batchName: Middle Republic: Hannibal in Italy (241-216 BCE) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Middle Republic: Hannibal in Italy (241-216 BCE)

questions.question: In 238 BC Rome broke its treaty with Carthage to seize which islands?
questions.explanation: Rome seized Carthaginian Sardinia and Corsica while Carthage was distracted by the Truceless War. Many Carthaginians were deeply embittered by this.
questions.sourceQuote: In 238 BC it broke the treaty and seized Carthaginian Sardinia and Corsica.

questions.question: Under which ruler did the historian Livy write?
questions.explanation: Livy wrote in Rome under Augustus and leaned heavily on Polybius. He was openly patriotic, and his battle descriptions are often inaccurate.
questions.sourceQuote: Livy, writing in Rome under the emperor Augustus, relied heavily on Polybius but was openly patriotic.

questions.question: What did Hannibal seize at Cannae in spring 216 BC, prompting Rome to raise a huge army?
questions.explanation: Hannibal captured a large Roman supply depot at Cannae, a village in Apulia. The Senate answered with the biggest army Rome had ever raised.
questions.sourceQuote: In spring 216 BC Hannibal seized a large Roman supply depot at Cannae, a village on the plain of Apulia in south-east Italy.

questions.question: How did the Roman Senate respond to Hannibal's peace offer after Cannae?
options: It refused to talk and banned the word 'peace'
It asked for a one-year truce
It sent Varro to negotiate terms
questions.explanation: The Senate refused to negotiate, banned the word 'peace' and even enlisted slaves. Rome went on fighting for fourteen more years.
questions.sourceQuote: The Senate refused to talk, banned the word 'peace' and enlisted even slaves.

questions.question: How long did Hannibal's crossing of the Alps take?
questions.explanation: Hannibal crossed the Alps in 15 days in late autumn. Along the way his men faced ambushes, falling boulders and bitter cold.
questions.sourceQuote: Hannibal reached the Alps in late autumn and crossed them in 15 days.

questions.question: What mocking nickname did Romans give Fabius Maximus?
questions.explanation: Fabius was mocked as the Delayer (Cunctator) for refusing to fight a pitched battle. Events later vindicated his cautious strategy.
questions.sourceQuote: Soldiers, senators and ordinary citizens mocked him as the Delayer (*Cunctator*).

questions.question: What did the nickname 'Barca', given to Hannibal's father, mean?
questions.explanation: Barca meant 'lightning'. Hannibal's father crushed the mercenary revolt in 237 BC and then led his army to Spain.
questions.sourceQuote: Hannibal's father, a Carthaginian general nicknamed Barca, meaning 'lightning', crushed the mercenary revolt in 237 BC.

questions.question: Where was most of the First Punic War between Rome and Carthage fought?
questions.explanation: The First Punic War was fought mostly on and around Sicily, and losing it cost Carthage its Sicilian possessions. It was also the greatest naval war of the ancient world.
questions.sourceQuote: The First Punic War, fought mostly on and around Sicily, had been the longest continuous conflict and the greatest naval war of the ancient world.

questions.question: According to Polybius, which kind of Alpine pass did Hannibal take?
questions.explanation: Polybius says Hannibal took the highest pass. That supports the Col de la Traversette, the highest pass in the western Alps.
questions.sourceQuote: Polybius wrote that Hannibal took the highest pass, and the Traversette is the highest in the western Alps.

questions.question: Why did Hannibal invade Italy by land rather than by sea?
options: To collect Greek allies at Massalia
The Senate had closed Italy's ports
To avoid Rome's control of the sea
questions.explanation: Rome controlled the sea, so Hannibal marched overland. Rome had planned to fight in Spain and Africa instead.
questions.sourceQuote: Hannibal instead carried the war to Italy by land, avoiding Rome's control of the sea.
